report.source_text: MRI of the head showed multiple cystic space-occupying lesions in the posterior fossa (figure 9) and a well-circumscribed mass on the right optic nerve in the optic canal (figure 10). Since we suspected it to be a VHL disease, the most probable diagnosis was thought to be an optic nerve haemangioblastoma. MRI also showed bilateral enlarged kidneys with variable sized cortical cysts and a soft tissue space-occupying lesion in the mid part of left kidney (figure 11). A soft tissue lesion in the retroperitoneum, located in the right paramedian aspect of the L5 vertebra, is suggestive of an extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her late 30s presented with 6 months of decreased vision in both eyes, with a history of brain surgery for cyst resection 7 years prior and a family history of similar complaints in her deceased brother. Ophthalmological examination revealed bilateral papilledema, bilateral optic nerve head hemangioblastoma, peripheral retinal hemangioblastoma in the left eye, and epiretinal membrane with pseudohole in the right eye. MRI of the head showed multiple cystic space-occupying lesions in the posterior fossa and a mass on the right optic nerve, suggestive of optic nerve hemangioblastoma. MRI also revealed bilateral enlarged kidneys with cortical cysts, a soft tissue lesion in the left kidney, and a retroperitoneal lesion suggestive of an extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma. These findings strongly supported a clinical diagnosis of VHL disease. The patient initially did not seek advised treatment and subsequently presented with worsening vision.
